outcome: The general conjecture (for every graph H, an H-free graph on n vertices has a clique or stable set of size at least n^c(H)) is still open in every source I read. Since 26 January 2024 it has moved only by restricted cases and reformulations: a 2024 equivalence with the polynomial Rödl and Nikiforov conjectures (no new graph H), two 2026 preprints adding specific six-vertex graphs (Huang–Ju–Zhou: the E-graph and the Bird graph; Tran–Nguyen: one further six-vertex graph), and a 2026 sharpening of the exponent for graphs of bounded VC-dimension (Sun–Wang–Zeng). The five-vertex case was completed by Nguyen–Scott–Seymour, whose first arXiv version (23 Dec 2023) predates the window; its journal version appeared in 2026.
problem_asks: (1) Quantifier over H: for every graph H, not only for particular H or classes of H. (2) Existence of a constant c(H) > 0, depending only on H, such that (3) every n-vertex graph with no induced copy of H contains a clique or an independent set (stable set) of at least n^c(H) vertices. The substance is that the exponent is positive and polynomial in n for every H; Wikipedia's January 2024 wording is 'For any graph H is there some c = c(H) > 0 such that every graph G on n vertices that does not contain H as an induced subgraph contains either a complete graph or independent set on >= n^c vertices.' Equivalent forms in the sources: H-free graphs contain a polynomial-size perfect induced subgraph; H-free graphs contain a polynomial-size homogeneous set.

events.what_happened: Erdős and Hajnal, 'Ramsey-type theorems' (1989, as cited by erdosproblems.com and Wikipedia): every H-free graph on n vertices has a clique or stable set of size exp(c_H sqrt(log n)); the conjecture holds for graphs H with at most 4 vertices and for cographs. Wikipedia dates the posing of the problem to a 1977 paper ('On spanned subgraphs of graphs'), which I did not open; see disputes.
events.delivers: Weak bound exp(c_H sqrt(log n)) for every fixed H, and the full conjecture for H on at most 4 vertices and for cograph H (both as stated by erdosproblems.com #61 and Wikipedia; the 1989 paper itself was not opened).
events.remains: The polynomial bound for every H; the conjecture for all H on five or more vertices, apart from the cases listed in later events.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture's qualitative form (a homogeneous set exists) but gives only a sub-polynomial exponent.

events.what_happened: Alon, Pach and Solymosi (Combinatorica, 2001, as cited by erdosproblems.com #61 and Wikipedia): the class of H for which the conjecture holds is closed under substitution (replacing a vertex by a module), so it suffices to treat prime H; they also show the conjecture is equivalent to a statement about tournaments.
events.delivers: Reduction: if the conjecture holds for H1 and H2 it holds for the substitution of H2 into a vertex of H1. Hence all cases reduce to prime H. Also an equivalence with a tournament version (both per secondary sources; the paper was not opened).
events.remains: Every prime H not already covered; the conjecture in full.
events.direction: Structural reduction; neither supports nor contradicts the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Chudnovsky and Safra, bull-free graphs satisfy the conjecture (JCTB 2008, as cited by erdosproblems.com #61 and Wikipedia; paper not opened).
events.delivers: The conjecture for H = bull (a five-vertex graph).
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for one H.

events.what_happened: Fox, Pach and Suk, bounded VC-dimension: every n-vertex graph of VC-dimension at most d has a clique or independent set of size e^((log n)^(1-o(1))) (arXiv 1710.03745, Oct 2017; published Discrete & Computational Geometry 2019 per a search excerpt). Not opened; described from search excerpts and from the 2023 NSS abstract.
events.delivers: Near-polynomial bound for graphs of bounded VC-dimension, with the dependence on d hidden in the o(1) term.
events.remains: Polynomial bound for bounded VC-dimension (later delivered by NSS VI); the conjecture for H-free graphs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture's qualitative form for bounded VC-dimension classes; not polynomial.

events.what_happened: Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour and Spirkl, 'Erdős–Hajnal for graphs with no 5-hole', arXiv 2102.04994 (v1 9 Feb 2021; published Proc. London Math. Soc., 2023, per a search excerpt). Abstract page opened; the body was not read.
events.delivers: The conjecture for H = C5 (the five-cycle), and, per the paper's own description in the search excerpt, for H the complement of a forest when C is a cycle. Abstract page confirms the C5 statement only.
events.remains: Every H other than the cases listed.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for one H (C5).

events.what_happened: Blanco and Bucić, 'Towards the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for P5-free graphs' (arXiv 2210.10755, v1 19 Oct 2022; v2 26 Oct 2023). Shows every P5-free n-vertex graph has a clique or independent set of size 2^(Ω((log n)^(2/3))). Abstract page opened. A search excerpt says it appeared in Research in the Mathematical Sciences in March 2024; the arXiv page lists no journal reference, so that is unverified.
events.revisions: v2 26 Oct 2023 (content not compared with v1).
events.delivers: A quasi-polynomial bound for H = P5 (not the polynomial bound the conjecture asks for). Superseded for P5 by NSS VII.
events.remains: Polynomial bound for P5, and everything else.
events.direction: Partial progress toward the conjecture for one H; a weaker bound than the conjecture requires.

events.what_happened: Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraph density. IV. New graphs with the Erdős–Hajnal property', arXiv 2307.06455 (v1 12 Jul 2023; v2 23 Jul 2023; v3 3 Mar 2024; v4 18 Apr 2026, 'accepted version'). Abstract page opened. Shows an infinite family of prime graphs H has the Erdős–Hajnal property; the family is described in the abstract as graphs in which every prime induced subgraph G' on at least three vertices has a vertex of degree one and a vertex of degree |G'| − 2, and infinitely many of these are prime. Search excerpt says accepted in Trans. AMS (2026); unverified.
events.delivers: The conjecture for every H in an infinite family of prime graphs defined by the degree condition above (restricted to that family).
events.remains: Every H outside that family, and the conjecture in general.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for an infinite family of H; the family is specific, not general.

events.what_happened: Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraph density. V. All paths approach Erdős–Hajnal', arXiv 2307.15032 (July 2023; revised October 2024 per a search excerpt). Not opened; described from search excerpts.
events.delivers: For every path P: every P-free graph has a clique or stable set of size 2^((log n)^(1-o(1))). Quasi-polynomial, not polynomial, and for paths only.
events.remains: Polynomial bound for every path; the conjecture for all other H.
events.direction: Supports a weakened form for paths; not the polynomial form asked.

events.what_happened: Bucić, Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraph density. I. A loglog step towards Erdős–Hajnal', arXiv 2301.10147 (January 2023). A search excerpt says the Oxford and Princeton copies are dated 17 Sept 2022 and the arXiv version is later; the exact first date is not pinned down. Not opened; described from search excerpts. Search excerpt says published in IMRN 2024 (unverified).
events.revisions: Oxford and Princeton copies dated 17 Sep 2022 (search excerpt); revised February 2024 (Oxford copy, per excerpt).
events.delivers: For every H, an H-free graph on at least two vertices has a clique or stable set of size 2^(c sqrt(log n log log n)). Improves the 1989 general bound; not polynomial.
events.remains: Polynomial bound for every H; the conjecture in full.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture's qualitative form for all H; sub-polynomial exponent.

events.what_happened: Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraph density. VI. Bounded VC-dimension', arXiv 2312.15572 (v1 25 Dec 2023; v2 22 Jan 2024; v3 10 Sep 2025). Abstract page opened. Confirms the Fox–Pach–Suk conjecture: for every d > 0 there is c > 0 such that every n-vertex graph of VC-dimension at most d has a clique or stable set of size at least n^c. Abstract also states the NIP consequence (Chernikov–Starchenko–Thomas). Journal version Advances in Mathematics 482 (2025) 110601 per a search excerpt; the arXiv page lists no journal reference. Search excerpts also report consequences for two-colourable tournaments and uniform hypergraphs of bounded VC-dimension (not verified by opening the paper).
events.revisions: v2 22 Jan 2024 (still before the 26 Jan 2024 freeze); v3 10 Sep 2025.
events.delivers: The conjecture's polynomial form for every class of graphs of bounded VC-dimension (a class-level statement, not a statement about each H-free class). Whether any fixed-H-free class has bounded VC-dimension is not established in my sources.
events.remains: The statement for H-free graphs in general, as the problem asks it; the result does not, on its face, cover every H.

checked_by.who: Advances in Mathematics (journal of record) and its referees, who are not named in my sources
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for volume 482 (2025), per a search excerpt of the ORA record; I did not open the ORA record.

events.direction: Supports the conjecture for every bounded-VC-dimension class (the Fox–Pach–Suk question); not a counterexample and not a claim about all H.

events.what_happened: Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 'Induced subgraph density. VII. The five-vertex path', arXiv 2312.15333 (v1 23 Dec 2023; v2 8 Apr 2025; v3 23 Feb 2026). Abstract page opened; body read to Section 7 only. Proves the conjecture for H = P5, which the abstract says completes verification for all five-vertex graphs (together with the bull, C5 and the substitution closure). Published in Proc. London Math. Soc. 132(3), e70133 (2026), per a search excerpt of the author's publication page; the arXiv abstract page lists no journal reference.
events.revisions: v2 8 Apr 2025; v3 23 Feb 2026 (abstract page). A search excerpt gives 27 Jan 2026 for the revision, which conflicts with the abstract page; I use the abstract page.
events.delivers: The conjecture for H = P5 (every P5-free n-vertex graph has a clique or stable set of size at least n^c for some c > 0). Completes the conjecture for all graphs H on five vertices, given the earlier cases and the substitution closure.
events.remains: The conjecture for every H on six or more vertices that is not covered by later events, and the general statement.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (journal of record) and its referees, not named in my sources
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for volume 132, issue 3 (2026), per a search excerpt of the author's publication page; I did not open that page.

events.direction: Supports the conjecture for H = P5.

events.what_happened: Bucić, Fox and Pham, 'Equivalence between Erdős–Hajnal and polynomial Rödl and Nikiforov conjectures', arXiv 2403.08303 (v1 13 Mar 2024; v2 19 Apr 2024). Abstract and introduction read. Proves that the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture, the polynomial Rödl conjecture (Fox–Sudakov) and the polynomial Nikiforov conjecture (Nguyen–Scott–Seymour) are equivalent for every H; the introduction adds equivalence with being viral.
events.delivers: A reformulation: for every H, H has the Erdős–Hajnal property if and only if it has the polynomial Rödl property if and only if it is viral. It does not establish any H, so it settles no instance of the problem by itself.
events.remains: The whole problem as stated; its equivalent forms are open together with it.
events.direction: Neither supports nor contradicts the conjecture; it is an equivalence.

events.what_happened: Arnold, Gishboliner and Sudakov, 'Two Erdős–Hajnal-type theorems for forbidden order-size pairs', arXiv 2406.04154 (June 2024). Not opened; described from search excerpts. About hypergraphs with forbidden order-size pairs, not graphs with a forbidden induced subgraph.
events.delivers: Hypergraph homogeneous-set bounds for r-graphs with forbidden (vertex count, edge count) pairs. Different object (hypergraphs) and different forbidden structure (order-size pairs). Discounted.
events.remains: The graph problem as stated, which this does not touch.
events.direction: Neither supports nor contradicts the graph conjecture; a neighbouring hypergraph question.

events.what_happened: Tomáš Hons, 'A Polynomial Ramsey Statement for Bounded VC-dimension', arXiv 2502.20461 (v1 27 Feb 2025; v2 23 Nov 2025; comments: to appear in European Journal of Combinatorics). Abstract page opened. Uses the NSS bounded-VC Erdős–Hajnal result to give polynomial dependence in a Ramsey statement of Ding, Oporowski, Oxley and Vertigan.
events.delivers: Polynomial dependence in an induced-matching / co-matching / half-graph Ramsey statement for bounded-VC-dimension graphs. A different statement; it uses the Erdős–Hajnal result for bounded VC-dimension but does not prove any Erdős–Hajnal instance. Discounted.
events.direction: Neither supports nor contradicts the conjecture; it applies an existing bounded-VC result to another question.

events.what_happened: Tung Nguyen, 'On polynomially high-chromatic pure pairs', arXiv 2504.21127 (April 2025; v3 per a search excerpt). Not opened; described from a search excerpt, which says it uses the P5 theorem.
events.revisions: v3 per search excerpt (date not seen).
events.delivers: Per the search excerpt: every P5-free graph with clique number at least 2 contains a complete pair of induced subgraphs with polynomially related chromatic numbers. A chromatic statement about P5-free graphs, not a clique-or-stable-set statement. Discounted.
events.direction: Neither supports nor contradicts the conjecture; it uses the P5 result.

events.what_happened: A user 'sammausberg' posted on the erdosproblems.com #61 forum thread (25 Apr 2026) shared notes with 'local results' around the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture, stating they are not claiming a proof and cannot guarantee novelty. Claimed items: (a) for m > 4, certain singleton-cut rows have ladder index at most 2, so a cover needs at least ceil((m+1)/2) cells; (b) for k at least 6, a first-splitter construction G_k(R) is P_k-free iff the bipartite interface R is P_k-free; (c) for a prime H with a mixed ordering, two-anchor splitting does not synchronise to a transversal copy of H; (d) a coordinatewise split replacement does synchronise under stated parameter conditions; (e) for rectangle traces, a finite F is shattered iff (V(F), F) is a star forest. Read through the thread's WebFetch summary; the notes themselves were not opened.
events.delivers: None of the listed items is stated as a bound on c(H) for all H, or a resolution of any named H. They are local partial results whose scope the poster does not claim beyond the stated parameters. Discounted, subject to the poster's notes.

checked_by.what_they_did: Ran a 'standard check' on the notes and reported no issues; the link given is a ChatGPT share page, so the check appears to be an AI model, not a human reading.

machine_checked.system: Lean (version not stated); the poster says Codex helped formalise some finite statements and links Lean formalisations, which I did not open

events.doubts: The poster says the notes 'were developed with substantial AI assistance over many sessions' and asks for scrutiny of specific theorems. No human expert has checked them in the sources I read. The one 'check' is an AI-based check via a share link.
events.direction: Not a claim of resolution; partial local statements, which the poster disclaims as proofs of the conjecture.

systems.name: Codex
systems.what_it_did: Per the poster: helped formalise some of the finite statements in Lean. The poster also says the notes as a whole were developed with substantial AI assistance, without naming a system for that. Formalising finite statements is support work under §5.4, not load-bearing mathematics on its face; whether the AI-assisted notes contain load-bearing AI-generated mathematics is not established.
systems.basis_quote: Codex helped me formalize some of the finite statements in Lean.

events.what_happened: Shenwei Huang, Yiao Ju and Yidong Zhou, 'Erdős-Hajnal conjecture beyond five-vertex graphs', arXiv 2606.06258. Versions: v1 4 Jun 2026; v2 8 Jun 2026; v3 31 Aug 2026 (comment: 'The proof now does not use the result on the five-vertex path and minor corrections are made'). Abstract page opened; HTML read to partway through Section 6.2 (Bird), in the proof of Claim 6.5.1; the acknowledgements were not reached. Abstract: a framework (iterative sparsification with 'comb'-based and generalised-niceness conditions) recovers the NSS five-vertex-path result and the Chudnovsky–Safra bull result, and proves the conjecture for two new six-vertex graphs, the E-graph and the Bird graph, which are the first two six-vertex graphs whose validity does not follow from known operations. The forum poster describes the E-graph as P5 with a pendant edge on the middle vertex (poster's description, not checked against the paper). One search excerpt gives a different title, 'Erdős–Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path', in a later paper's reference list.
events.revisions: v1 4 Jun 2026; v2 8 Jun 2026; v3 31 Aug 2026 (proof no longer uses the five-vertex path result; minor corrections).
events.delivers: The Erdős–Hajnal property for two specific six-vertex graphs: the E-graph and the Bird graph. The framework also recovers the P5 and bull cases as special cases. Restricted to these two graphs and the framework's scope.
events.remains: The conjecture for every other graph H, including the rest of the six-vertex graphs and the general statement.

checked_by.who: Viet-Hoang Tran and Tan M. Nguyen
checked_by.qualification: Researchers in this area and authors of a later preprint that uses this framework
checked_by.what_they_did: Used the HJZ definitions and framework inside their own proof (arXiv 2608.28551 abstract). Their paper does not say they re-verified the HJZ argument.
Posted a pointer to the arXiv paper and a one-line description of the E-graph claim on 5 Jun 2026. No verification.

events.doubts: (1) Three versions in three months, and the v3 comment says the proof was changed to remove its dependence on the P5 result and that minor corrections were made. (2) A search excerpt of the Tran–Nguyen preprint's acknowledgements, which I could not open, thanks 'Viet Hoang and his coauthors' for pointing out a gap in an earlier version of the proof of one lemma (Lemma 2.8 in the excerpt). Unverified; the HJZ acknowledgements were not reached. (3) No referee report or journal acceptance found. None of these is a demonstrated error.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for two specific six-vertex graphs (positive direction).

events.what_happened: Shuang Sun, Yan Wang and Jiasheng Zeng, 'A Single-Exponential Erdős–Hajnal Bound for Graphs of Bounded VC-Dimension', arXiv 2607.09049 (v1 10 Jul 2026 only). Abstract page and HTML read (the HTML read to the references, around reference [21]). Main result: for a graph G of VC-dimension at most d, max{ω(G), α(G)} ≥ |G|^((Cd)^(−d)) for an absolute constant C, improving the NSS dependence 2^(−2^(O(d))) on d. Acknowledgements name only national funding.
events.delivers: A sharper exponent for the bounded-VC-dimension class: a quantitative improvement on a restricted class, which the NSS result had already covered qualitatively. Nothing for H-free graphs in general, as far as the abstract shows.
events.remains: The conjecture for every H-free class, as the problem asks; the bounded-VC class is a separate hypothesis.
events.direction: Supports the bounded-VC result quantitatively; neither supports nor contradicts the H-free conjecture.

events.what_happened: Viet-Hoang Tran and Tan M. Nguyen, 'The Erdős–Hajnal Property for the six-vertex Graph with Edge Set {ab,bc,cd,de,af,bf,df}', arXiv 2608.28551 (v1 28 Aug 2026 only). Abstract page opened; the arXiv PDF returned binary to my tool and the HTML truncated before the acknowledgements. Abstract: proves the graph with edges ab, bc, cd, de, af, bf, df (six vertices a–f) has the Erdős–Hajnal property, by adapting the iterative sparsification of NSS within the comb-based framework of HJZ. This graph contains an induced P5 (a–b–c–d–e); I did not establish whether it is the E-graph or the Bird graph, and the abstract presents it as a separate graph. AI: the acknowledgements, as reported in two independent search excerpts (not opened), name GPT-5.6 Sol and an agentic harness built around GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5; see ai.
events.delivers: The Erdős–Hajnal property for one specific six-vertex graph (edges ab, bc, cd, de, af, bf, df), via the HJZ framework.
events.remains: The conjecture for every other H, including all other six-vertex graphs and the general statement.
events.doubts: Depends on the HJZ framework, so any error there would propagate; no independent check found. Single version, about six weeks old. No human referee or journal found.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for one six-vertex graph (positive direction).

disputes.summary: Origin date of the conjecture: Wikipedia says Erdős and Hajnal first posed it as an open problem in a 1977 paper ('On spanned subgraphs of graphs'); the Chudnovsky survey and the erdosproblems.com entry date the conjecture to their 1989 paper ('Ramsey-type theorems'). I did not open either original paper; the record does not pick one.

Revision date of NSS VII (P5): the arXiv abstract page lists v3 on 23 Feb 2026; a search excerpt gives 'revised January 27, 2026' and an acceptance date of 23 Feb 2026. I use the abstract page for the arXiv version; the window classification is unchanged because v1 (23 Dec 2023) is the dated event.

The arXiv title of 2606.06258 is 'Erdős-Hajnal conjecture beyond five-vertex graphs'; a search excerpt of a later paper's reference list gives 'Erdős–Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path' for the same preprint (v2 dated 8 June 2026). Same arXiv identifier; I record the arXiv title.

summary: The general conjecture is open in every source I read: the Wikipedia article says 'As of 2024, however, the full conjecture has not been proven, and remains an open problem', and the erdosproblems.com #61 page (last edited 10 April 2026) lists only specific graphs as proved. Since 26 January 2024, what has moved is (i) a reformulation, Bucić–Fox–Pham (arXiv 2403.08303, 13 Mar 2024), equivalent to the polynomial Rödl and Nikiforov forms with no new graph H; (ii) two 2026 preprints adding specific six-vertex graphs: Huang–Ju–Zhou (arXiv 2606.06258; v1 4 Jun 2026, v3 31 Aug 2026) for the E-graph and the Bird graph, and Tran–Nguyen (arXiv 2608.28551; 28 Aug 2026) for the graph with edges ab, bc, cd, de, af, bf, df, built on the HJZ framework; and (iii) Sun–Wang–Zeng (arXiv 2607.09049; 10 Jul 2026), a sharper exponent for the bounded-VC-dimension class, which is a restricted class rather than H-free graphs. The 2026 journal versions of the NSS papers (P5 in PLMS; bounded VC in Advances in Mathematics 2025) are not new results: their first public arXiv versions (P5: 23 Dec 2023; bounded VC: 25 Dec 2023) predate the window, and I have dated them to those versions as instructed. The P5 result completes the conjecture for all five-vertex graphs, which I record as a pre-window event. Close calls: (a) whether single-H cases count as moving the problem: the problem asks for every H, so each event settles one H or one class and leaves the rest open, and the judging pass should decide how to count them; (b) whether the bounded-VC results touch H-free classes at all depends on whether fixed-H-free classes have bounded VC-dimension, which I did not establish; (c) for the Tran–Nguyen paper, the AI credit is the close call that matters most here. Its acknowledgements, as quoted in two independent search excerpts, credit GPT-5.6 Sol and an agentic harness built around it, plus Claude Fable 5, for literature search, hypothesis testing, exploring and ruling out approaches, wording and proofreading. I could not open the acknowledgements (the arXiv PDF returned binary to my tool and the HTML truncates before them), so this rests on excerpts and is not verbatim. I have recorded it as a candidate in ai.systems with that caveat; whether the AI-run hypothesis testing and exploration of approaches produced load-bearing mathematics is for the full text to show. The Huang–Ju–Zhou paper's readable text, through part of Section 6.2 (Bird), names no AI, but its acknowledgements were not reached. Separately, an erdosproblems.com forum thread for #61 has an AI-assisted notes post (25 Apr 2026): the poster says the notes were 'developed with substantial AI assistance over many sessions' and that Codex helped formalise some finite statements in Lean; the poster disclaims a proof, and one reply reports a 'standard check' (via a ChatGPT share link) with no issues. None of these is a proof of the general conjecture. I found no AI-credited proof of the general conjecture and no withdrawal, retraction or erratum. Other AI results in this period (OpenAI's planar unit distance disproof, GPT-5.2 Pro with Aristotle on Erdős #728, July 2026 cycle double cover claim) concern other problems. Tung Nguyen's PhD thesis, which a forum post summarises as containing several of these results, was not opened.
competing_reading: Read 2026 as real acceleration. NSS VII completes all five-vertex graphs, and two 2026 preprints extend a shared framework to new six-vertex graphs in quick succession, with the sharpened bounded-VC exponent on top. On that reading the problem is moving through a systematic programme, and an AI-assisted case (Tran–Nguyen, if the excerpt is right) would be one of its contributors. Against this: each event settles one H or one restricted class, and the problem asks for every H, so none changes the general status; and the 2026 six-vertex preprints are young, have no referee reports, and one of them depends on the framework of the other.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of 2608.28551, including its acknowledgements, verbatim: which systems are named, and whether the AI produced any of the mathematics (for example the framework's key lemma or the case analysis) rather than checking or searching. (2) The full text of 2606.06258 past Section 6, including the acknowledgements, and the 'gap in an earlier version' claim in its acknowledgements. (3) Journal or referee status for HJZ and Tran–Nguyen. (4) Whether the HJZ/Tran–Nguyen framework covers infinitely many H or a reduction to a finite list (would change how far these events move the problem). (5) Whether any fixed-H-free class has bounded VC-dimension (decides whether the bounded-VC results touch H-free classes). (6) Any status change on erdosproblems.com #61 or the Wikipedia article after 26 Oct 2026, the cut-off for my search.
